title: Nifty Clings to Support as Fed Decision and $104 Crude Set the Week's Direction
excerpt: After five straight weekly losses, the index holds near the 23,000–23,300 support band with the Fed's September 16 call and elevated oil prices set to decide what comes next.
body:
• The Nifty 50 enters a holiday-shortened week at 23,398.10 after a fifth consecutive weekly loss — down over 2% on the week and about 4.8% over five weeks, hovering near the critical 23,000–23,300 support band.
  • The week's main trigger is the US Federal Reserve's rate decision and economic projections, due Wednesday, September 16, with markets pricing in a high probability of a 25-basis-point hike after hot inflation data.
  • Brent crude settled at $104.61 a barrel after briefly approaching $110, as attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi threats to Red Sea shipping keep energy prices elevated.
  • Sector rotation favored defensives — healthcare and pharma led gains while IT slumped 5.8% in its worst week since April and real estate corrected on rising yields.

Indian equity markets enter a holiday-shortened week with the Nifty 50 clinging to a crucial support zone. The index ended Friday at 23,398.10, down 79.70 points or 0.34%, while the BSE Sensex closed at 74,781.76, down 120.83 points or 0.16%. Both benchmarks fell more than 2% on the week — the fifth straight weekly loss — and have shed roughly 4.8% over the last five weeks. With markets closed Monday for Ganesh Chaturthi, Tuesday's session will be the first chance for investors to react to weekend moves in crude, bond yields and Fed expectations.

The weakness was broad. The Nifty touched a three-month low during the week. Nifty Bank fell for a third consecutive week, the Midcap index declined for a second straight week, and fourteen of the 16 major sectors logged weekly losses. Realty was the biggest loser; healthcare and pharma were the bright spots. The rupee weakened 1% on the week — its sharpest drop since mid-May.

Fed decision in focus

The US Federal Reserve's interest rate decision and updated economic projections, due Wednesday, September 16 at 2:00 pm EDT (11:30 pm IST), will be the week's principal global catalyst. Markets are pricing in a high probability of a 25-basis-point hike after the September 11 CPI report showed headline inflation rising 0.4% month-on-month and holding at 3.4% annually. Core inflation rose 0.3% on the month but eased to 2.4% year-on-year.

According to Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, founder and CEO of HST Wealth, the September 15–16 FOMC meeting is the week's defining event. "A rate hike accompanied by hawkish economic projections could strengthen the dollar, tighten global financial conditions and place further pressure on emerging-market equities, foreign flows and the rupee," he said. An unchanged rate — or a hike paired with balanced forward guidance — could trigger a relief rally if investors read the outcome as less restrictive than feared. The Bank of England and Bank of Japan also announce policy decisions this week.

Crude remains the central variable

Brent crude settled at $104.61 a barrel after briefly approaching $110, as the six-month-old West Asia conflict intensified. Iran said it attacked 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz after the US sank five Iranian oil tankers, while Houthi forces threatened Saudi oil exports in the Red Sea. For India, the world's third-largest oil importer, sustained prices above $100 mean a wider import bill, inflationary pressure, a weaker rupee and squeezed corporate margins.

"Crude sustaining above the USD 100 per barrel mark, on continued hostilities and retaliatory action in West Asia, remained the central variable through the week," said Vinod Nair, head of research at Geojit Investments. He also flagged rising global bond yields, expectations of synchronized monetary tightening and the potential unwinding of yen-funded carry trades as factors weighing on risk appetite and emerging-market flows.

"Any renewed rise in crude, particularly if disruptions to Middle East oil flows intensify, could add to inflationary pressures, widen the import bill, weigh on the rupee and squeeze corporate margins."

— Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, Founder & CEO, HST Wealth

Defensives find favour

Sectoral rotation told the story of a risk-off market. Healthcare and pharma led gains — pharma has declined only about 1.3% from its August peak, emerging as the strongest defensive pocket. IT slumped 5.8%, its biggest weekly percentage drop since April, weighed down by prospects of a Fed hike that could curb client spending at firms dependent on US revenue. Real estate corrected as rising yields and funding costs bit. Heavyweight financials lost 1.9% on the week, with Reliance Industries, the third-highest weighted stock on the Nifty, dropping 4.9%.

The 23,000–23,300 zone in focus

Technically, the market remains fragile. The Nifty stays below its key daily moving averages and has repeatedly tested the 23,300 region since March without decisively breaking below it; 23,000 has also attracted buying interest. On the weekly chart, the index has reached its lower Bollinger Band, while weekly RSI readings remain in neutral territory — pressure, but not yet an extreme oversold condition. "The market's technical structure remains fragile," Radhakrishnan said.

What to watch

Domestic data — WPI inflation and trade figures — will show how much of the external pressure is filtering through to the economy. Nair expects elevated energy prices, foreign outflows and geopolitical uncertainty to keep volatility high, though resilient domestic fundamentals and institutional support could attract buying at lower levels. His near-term prescription: book partial profits where valuations are stretched and systematic risk is highest, redeploying into defensive and deep-value segments. As Nair put it, "the trajectory of crude" alongside the Fed's decision "will set the near-term direction."
image_caption: An Economic Times Markets illustration shows a bull and a bear facing off above a trading floor. The Nifty clung to key support as the week's direction hinged on the Fed decision and crude at $104.
nri_angle: For NRI portfolios with Indian equity exposure, the confluence of a potential Fed hike, $104 crude and a weakening rupee argues for defensive positioning — healthcare and pharma — until the week's macro catalysts clear.
